reasons.issue: Grammar defect in the briefing: 'YOU starts inside' (should be 'YOU start inside'), the standing 'YOU is/starts/has' subject-verb family error confirmed across 27+ prior packets and calibration-adjudication.md.
reasons.change: Corrected to 'YOU start inside' in the briefing.
reasons.evidence: AUTHORING-CONTRACT.md and RINKREADS-CLAUDE-PROJECT.md require natural 'YOU are/have/start' agreement. The briefing is shared scene context displayed with every linked question, so the fix cascades all 6 question hashes even though only q5's own text also changed.

reasons.issue: Briefing claims 'Gold 2 trails wide', but computed coordinates show Gold 2 (13,10) is 5m further along Gold 1's breakout direction (lower x, i.e. more advanced toward the neutral zone, not behind) than Gold 1 (18,6); only the 'wide' half (y=10 vs y=6) is accurate. Question q5 compounds this: its prompt called the hypothetical Gold-1-to-Gold-2 pass 'inside', but Gold 2's y=10 is farther from centre than Gold 1's y=6, the opposite of inside. The phrase 'Navy's blue line' in the briefing is also bank-wide unique (checked all 30 packet files; occurs nowhere else) and ambiguous about which blue line is meant, so it was simplified to the unqualified 'the blue line' already used by the scene's own cues and q1's option text.
reasons.change: Reworded the briefing to 'Gold 2 is positioned wide' (dropping the unsupported trailing/behind claim) and dropped 'Navy's' from 'the blue line'. Reworded q5's prompt to 'If Gold 1 passes to Gold 2, what deserves attention?' (dropping the unsupported 'inside' direction claim); the answer and explanation still hold without the directional word.
reasons.evidence: Computed g1=(18,6) facing 2.8rad vs g2=(13,10) facing 2.7rad: g2-g1=(-5,+4). Carried-puck formula independently verified: x=18+cos(2.8)-0.7*sin(2.8)=16.823, y=6+sin(2.8)+0.7*cos(2.8)=5.675, matching the stored puck position exactly, confirming the actor/facing data used for this computation is the live data, not a misread.

sourceChecks.scope: Read in full via curl with a browser User-Agent (200 OK; WebFetch alone returned 403). Confirms 'A Proper Angle' (push the attacker from 'good ice' in the middle to 'bad ice' at the perimeter, keep momentum back toward your own net, stick on ice, protect the middle) and 'Closing The Gap' (constant D movement, protect good ice, push opponent to bad ice). Directly supports exp26b-u13-011's inside-angle/wall teaching point and the general transition-defence framing of exp26b-u13-012. USA Hockey, general/youth-applicable (explicitly discusses youth-level angling), no specific age-band restriction stated.
